description: The Water Pig in Chinese astrology: personality, Water element traits, 1983 and 2043 dates and compatibility.
answer: In Chinese astrology, the Water Pig is the Pig born in a Water year, one of five versions of the twelfth animal. It combines the Pig's generosity with Water's qualities. Water Pig years between 1924 and 2044 are 1983 and 2043. The Pig's fixed element is Water.

sections.heading: The Water Pig personality
paragraphs: In the Water Pig, the year stem matches the animal's own element, because the Pig's fixed element is Water. Traditional readings describe this as the Pig's warmth and sincerity in their purest form: empathetic, intuitive, peaceable and deeply kind. Water Pigs are often portrayed as gentle diplomats who see the good in others and avoid conflict wherever possible. They tend to be imaginative, sensitive and generous with time and attention. Doubled Water deepens their emotional life. It can also make them overly trusting, prone to indecision and inclined to escape difficulties through comfort or avoidance. They are often the friend who remembers birthdays, notices sadness behind a smile and quietly makes room at the table for anyone who needs it.

In classical thought, Water belongs to the north and to the deep, resting energy of winter, the season when life gathers strength out of sight. As a year stem, it tends to make an animal more reflective, adaptable and emotionally attuned. People born under a Water stem are often described as clever negotiators, sensitive friends and natural mediators who prefer influence to force. They value understanding and tend to think before they act. The caution traditionally attached to Water is fluidity taken too far: avoiding conflict, keeping too much hidden and losing a clear sense of their own direction.

sections.heading: Water Pig at work and in love
paragraphs: At work, Water is usually associated with communication, strategy and insight into people. Water-year people are often described as the ones who smooth negotiations, read what clients are really asking for and spot problems before they surface, which suits counselling, writing, diplomacy, research roles, marketing and the arts. They tend to adapt quickly to changing conditions. The traditional caution is a lack of firm boundaries: a Water stem may agree too readily, so clear goals and written commitments usually help it hold course.

Kindness and imagination shape the Water Pig's working life. Diplomacy, social services, the arts, hospitality and customer care suit it, because empathy and a knack for keeping the peace are valuable there. It tends to see the best in colleagues, smooths over tensions and quietly takes on extra work when someone is struggling. Firm deadlines and a candid manager help it turn goodwill into finished work. In close relationships the Water Pig is tender, forgiving and endlessly welcoming. It wants emotional sincerity and gentle handling. Friction usually arises from over-trust and avoidance: it may overlook warning signs, or postpone a needed conversation, because confrontation feels so much worse than mild discomfort.

sections.heading: Water Pig years and dates
paragraphs: Between 1924 and 2044 the Water Pig years are 1983 (February 13, 1983 to February 1, 1984) and 2043 (February 10, 2043 to January 29, 2044). Because the year begins at Lunar New Year, a birthday in January or early February needs checking: in 1983 anyone born before Feb 13 is a Water Dog, not a Water Pig. The combination returns every sixty years, since five elements cycle through twelve animals and only meet the same pairing again after five rounds of the zodiac. Every Water Pig year is Yin, matching the Pig's own polarity.

Chinese almanacs call the combination Gui-Hai, joining the heavenly stem Gui to the earthly branch Hai. Births just before each new year fall in the Water Dog year (before February 13, 1983) and the Water Dog year (before February 10, 2043), and births in the weeks after each Water Pig year ends belong to the Wood Rat. The new year itself fell on a Sunday in 1983 and Tuesday in 2043.

sections.heading: Growth edges and compatibility for the Water Pig
paragraphs: For Water Pigs, firm boundaries are a form of self-care. Learning to say no kindly but clearly protects their generous nature from being exploited. Setting deadlines for decisions prevents drift. Because they avoid conflict, small honest conversations, held early, prevent larger tensions later. Water Pigs often thrive in caring, creative or diplomatic roles. Structured routines give their fluid temperament a helpful framework. When kindness is backed by discernment, Water Pigs become cherished friends and calm, compassionate presences in any setting. Creative work, especially music or writing, gives their deep feelings a voice. It also helps to keep company with friends who are kind but frank.

For relationships, the classical structures belong to the animal rather than the element, so the Water Pig shares the Pig's San He trine with the Rabbit and Goat (the Wood trine), its Liu He bond with the Tiger, and its Liu Chong clash with the Snake. The element adds a second layer: another Water sign shares this year element, while partners whose year element feeds Water in the generating cycle are often described as supportive.

faq.question: What years are Water Pig years?
faq.answer: Between 1924 and 2044: 1983 (from February 13, 1983) and 2043 (from February 10, 2043). Each lasts until the day before the next Lunar New Year.

faq.question: What is the Water Pig's element relationship?
faq.answer: The year element is Water and the Pig's fixed element is Water; in the five-element cycles water year element matches the fixed element. Readings use that relationship to describe how easily the two sides of the sign sit together.

faq.question: Which animals are most compatible with the Water Pig?
faq.answer: Traditionally the Rabbit and Goat (San He) and the Tiger (Liu He). The Snake is the Liu Chong clash. These pairings depend on the animal, whatever the element.

faq.question: What is the Water Pig called in the Chinese calendar?
faq.answer: Gui-Hai. In almanacs and Four Pillars charts each year is named by its heavenly stem, here the Water stem Gui, followed by its earthly branch, here Hai for the Pig, so the name pins down both halves of the combination at once.

faq.question: How is the Water Pig different from other Pigs?
faq.answer: All Pigs share generosity, sincerity and warmth. The Water year element changes the tone: water is the element of winter, stillness and depth, and a Water year is traditionally said to give any animal intuition, flexibility and a gift for communication.
